tools.description: Returns the current leave balances for a given employee (India-specific). This tool retrieves leave balance details for an individual employee based in India for the current calendar year. The data includes available days across different leave types (e.g., sick leave, earned leave, paternity leave), and is loaded from the predefined CSV file `sample-data/employee_leave_balances.csv`. HR teams managing India operations or evaluating India leave data can use this to view an employee's current leave status. **Input:** - `employee_name` (str): Full name of the employee (case-insensitive matching recommended when implementing full system) **Returns:** A dictionary containing: - `employee_name`: The name of the employee - `year`: The current year - `leave_balances`: A dictionary of leave types and their available days, e.g.: { "sick_leave": {"available_days": 4, "note": "Refer to policy for applicability."}, "paternity_leave": {"available_days": 10, "note": "Refer to policy for applicability."} } If the employee is not found, a fallback message is returned in place of `leave_balances`. **Example Response:** { "employee_name": "Amit Sharma", "year": 2025, "leave_balances": { "sick_leave": {"available_days": 6, "note": "Refer to policy for applicability."}, "earned_leave": {"available_days": 12, "note": "Refer to policy for applicability."} } }

tools.name: Statistical_Analysis_MCP_welch_t_test
tools.description: Accepts two groups of numeric data as comma-separated strings or DataFrame columns and performs Welch's t-test. This test determines whether two independent groups have significantly different means. This test is valid even when populations have different variances. Default to this test instead of students t-test if you are unsure about population variance. This test calculates a t-statistic using Welch's formula that accounts for unequal variances. Given an alternative hypothesis (group1 ≠ group2, group1 < group2, or group1 > group2), it outputs the p-value: the probability of observing this result (or more extreme) if no true difference exists. Results are considered statistically significant when p-value < alpha (typically 0.05). Cohen's d measures practical effect size, calculated using pooled standard deviation for consistency with other t-tests, with interpretation: |d| < 0.2 = negligible, 0.2-0.5 = small, 0.5-0.8 = medium, >0.8 = large (custom thresholds may be used). EXAMPLE USE CASES: treatment vs control groups, before/after measurements with different participants, comparing performance between demographic groups.

tools.name: run_my_script_run_script
tools.description: Executes a user-provided self contained Python script inside an isolated virtual environment with automatic dependency management. This function is intended to serve as a backend execution engine in a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server setting, where a language model may submit scripts for evaluation. It creates a secure workspace, detects dependencies, installs them using `uv`, executes the script, captures its output (including stdout and generated files), and returns all relevant results. ⚠️ Limitations & Guidance for LLM-based Use: - Scripts should be self-contained, avoid system-level access, and primarily focus on data processing, text generation, visualization, or machine learning tasks. - The code can output logs, JSON, images, CSVs, or any other files, which are returned as artifacts. - Avoid infinite loops or long-running background processes. Timeout support can be added externally. Returns: , logs (str): Full stdout and stderr logs of the executed script., artifacts (Dict[str, str]): A dictionary of output files with their names and summaries or indicators, (e.g., image or CSV placeholders). Includes a "__workdir__" key pointing to the working directory., zip_path (str): Path to a ZIP archive containing all output artifacts for download.

tools.name: SmartEnterpriseMCPAgents_mcphawk_get_employee_profile

This tool retrieves the profile details for an individual employee, including role, cloud expertise, data warehouse tools, domain exposure, office location, gender, and other relevant attributes. This function is typically used in internal workforce management, reporting dashboards, or talent mapping systems within MCPHawk Inc to retrieve standardized employee data. **Input:** - `employee_name` (str): Full name of the employee (case-insensitive matching recommended) **Returns:** A dictionary containing: - `employee_name`: Name of the employee - `employee_profile`: A dictionary of profile details, such as: { "role": "Sr. DE", "cloud_experties": "AWS", "cloud_native_experties": "dbt", "dw_experties": "Snowflake", "domain_exposure": "Banking & Insurance", "office_location": "Bangalore", "date_of_joining": "2022-08-14", "gender": "Male", "allocation": "Billable", "resume": "resume_amit_sharma.png" } If the employee is not found, a fallback message is returned instead of the profile. **Example Response:** { "employee_name": "Amit Sharma", "employee_profile": { "role": "Sr. DE", "cloud_experties": "AWS", "cloud_native_experties": "dbt", "dw_experties": "Snowflake", "domain_exposure": "Banking & Insurance", "office_location": "Bangalore", "date_of_joining": "2022-08-14", "gender": "Male", "allocation": "Billable", "resume": "resume_amit_sharma.pdf" } }
